title: GitLab warns of critical RCE vulnerability in AI Gateway service
key_facts: GitLab warned customers on Friday 2 Oct 2026 to patch a critical flaw (CVE-2026-90970) in its AI Gateway, the service behind its AI-native GitLab Duo features.
It could let an authenticated user with Duo Agent Platform access escape the prompt template sandbox through a crafted flow configuration and run arbitrary commands on the AI Gateway.
Fixed versions are 19.2.4, 19.3.2 and 19.4.1 for self-hosted AI Gateway users.
Customers using GitLab's own cloud AI Gateway are already protected; GitLab contacted self-hosted customers before the public notice.
Last month GitLab patched a separate maximum-severity flaw (CVE-2026-85706) that CISA listed as actively exploited the next day.
GitLab has over 30 million registered users and is used by over 50% of the Fortune 100.
quote_evidence: GitLab warned customers today to immediately patch a critical AI Gateway vulnerability that could let attackers run arbitrary commands on vulnerable instances.

Tracked as CVE-2026-90970, this security flaw stems from an improper neutralization weakness and can let attackers with basic privileges and Duo Agent Platform access execute arbitrary commands on unpatched instances.

GitLab released versions 19.2.4, 19.3.2, and 19.4.1 to address this vulnerability for Self-Hosted AI Gateway users and said that customers using a GitLab-hosted AI Gateway are already protected and do not need to take action.
why_it_matters_hint: A critical flaw in the AI part of a widely used coding platform needs patching, but only on self-hosted setups.
notes: Status CONFIRMED because it is GitLab's own advisory. The article reports no attacks using this flaw; the exploited flaw it mentions is a different, earlier one.
